Maya (CS): Quick ask — I'm building a one-page 'Go‑Live Shield' for low-touch customers covering onboarding health checks, renewal risk signals, and tactical prefill/batching/streaming tips. Want a short, operational checklist we can hand the customer + the CSM. Draft below, please comment with changes.

Priya (Eng): Love the idea. Keep the eng bits short. Suggest include: explicit batch_size examples, when to force synchronous vs streaming, and a simple metric to validate KV cache warmness.

Maya (CS): Draft section A: Account health quickchecks (to run 24h before go‑live) —
- Verify 95th pct latency under SLA for representative route
- Confirm warm pool has >=2 ready workers for tenant
- Spot-check embedding/response quality on 5 sample prompts
- Ensure telemetry is wired (latency, tokens per call, errors) and owner assigned @account-owner

Diego (PM): Add renewal-risk signals + action steps (very short):
- Signal 1: Weekly active sessions drop >30% vs baseline => Action: CS outreach + quick UX call, enable sampling telemetry.
- Signal 2: Avg token cost up >25% MOS (month-over-step) => Action: Suggest batch/quantization profile + cost review.
- Signal 3: Sustained increase in failed streams / client disconnects (>3%) => Action: open runbook, escalate to SRE and apply fallback model route.

Lina (SRE): Operational checklist and quick commands — keep cli examples minimal: 
- Check warm cache hit rate (last 1h): `redis-cli --stat` or our internal `ri telemetry query --metric=kv_cache_hit_rate --tenant=<TENANT> --range=1h`
- Validate worker readiness: `ri admin workers list --tenant <TENANT>` (expect >=2 ready)
- Quick deploy rollback: `ri deploy rollback --route <ROUTE>`
- If streaming errors spike: toggle `streaming.enabled=false` on route as temporary mitigation.

Lina (SRE): Sample thresholds to include in doc (editable):
- 95p latency target: < 350ms for short prompts (<=64 tokens), < 800ms for long flows
- KV cache hit rate target: >= 60% after warmup window
- Error rate: < 1% sustained

Sam (CS): Feedback capture + handoff flow (two bullets):
- During first 72h, attach short NPS-style ping to 10% of sessions + 1 free support call; route responses into the account ticket and tag `cs-feedback`.
- Capture qualitative notes in the shared Notion page + paste top 3 caller quotes in the weekly handoff Slack post. Template link: https://notion.redwood/example-go-live-feedback (editable)

Priya (Eng): Minimal tuning cheat-sheet to hand the customer (one-liners):
- If latency is high and cost ok => increase batching (max_batch_tokens=1024), set batch_timeout=40ms.
- If cost is high and latency ok => apply 8-bit quant profile + lower `max_tokens` where feasible.
- If streaming disconnects happen often => reduce concurrent_streams per connection to 2 and enable reconnect backoff (exp backoff up to 5s).

Maya (CS): Final section: Playbook run sequence for CSM (steps 1..6):
1) 48h out: run Account health quickchecks, ping eng and SRE if anything fails.
2) 24h out: ensure warm pool, run sample prompts, verify metrics dashboard shows green.
3) Go‑live window: CS oncall listens to `cs-feedback` channel; enable prefills for high-value flows.
4) 0–72h: sample 10% sessions for feedback, escalate any regression to internal triage.
5) 7 days: review usage, cost, quality; propose optimizations (batching, quant, route policy).
6) 30 days: renewal risk review — check signals above, schedule health call if >1 signal triggered.

Sam (CS): +1. I'll run the feedback template and draft the customer-facing one-pager. Want sign-off from @Priya and @Lina before we publish. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: Deployment: docs/go-live-shield v1 published by Maya.

Maya (CS): Thanks all — I'll update with your thresholds and post the final one-pager in this thread. If anyone wants a shorter 'bookmarkable' checklist for customers, tell me which items to trim. :sparkles:
